failure_patterns.pattern: endpoint_selection: Several calls used a topical or generic alternative instead of the endpoint matching the requested operation, item, or named source.

rejected_edits.content: For each selected endpoint, use only its own schema for exact parameter names, field semantics, and required/optional placement; never borrow fields from similar operations. To avoid scalar type mismatches in name/value calls, serialize according to the active answer contract: when it specifies or demonstrates string-valued `value` fields, encode scalar values as strings even for NUMBER and BOOLEAN fields (for example, `556` as `"556"` and `true` as `"true"`). Use JSON numbers or booleans only when the active contract requires typed primitives, and preserve documented compound-value encodings.
rejected_edits.target: For each selected endpoint, use only its own schema for exact parameter names, declared types, and required/optional placement; never borrow fields from similar operations.

rejected_edits.content: - For a required search-mode or entity-type selector, apply the same scope rule: on a general request, use the endpoint's documented broad/all choice rather than guessing a restrictive subtype; use a subtype when the request identifies it. If no documented broad choice exists, do not fabricate one—choose another fitting endpoint or omit the call if the required value cannot be grounded.
rejected_edits.target: - For optional search-mode or entity-type selectors, use the documented choice that matches an entity class or mode clearly identified in the request, even if the user did not phrase it as a filter. Do not choose an arbitrary restrictive value for another selector dimension the user left unspecified; omit it, or use a documented all/any value only when needed to express the requested scope.
